integrated_multimodal_description: A realistic top-down aerial view of a commercial poultry barn interior. The camera looks straight down at a flock of dozens of fluffy pale-yellow baby chicks scattered across a floor covered in dark brown wood-shaving bedding. Long parallel lines of red-and-yellow plastic feeders (red conical drinkers mounted on yellow trays) run diagonally across the frame, casting soft shadows on the floor. The young chicks move naturally and unpredictably: several peck at the ground in short, rapid head-bobs foraging for spilled feed; others take a few quick steps between feeders; a few stand still with heads tilted, looking around; one or two briefly huddle together before separating again. Their tiny shifting shadows track each bird as it moves. The overhead industrial structure — metal rafters, hanging water lines, feeder suspension cables, and fluorescent tubes — frames the upper edge of the visible floor area as seen from directly above. Lighting is even, slightly warm, and naturalistic, typical of an indoor broiler house. The camera holds a stable top-down position with a very slow, smooth drift to keep the flock centered. Chicks exhibit varied, organic trajectories with no synchronized movement, producing a dense, naturalistic motion field ideal for evaluating computer-vision multi-object tracking algorithms.

overall_soundscape: Continuous ambient barn sound: the soft constant peeping and chirping of a large flock of young chicks, occasional short clucks, the faint rustle of wood shavings under tiny feet, and a low-frequency hum of ventilation equipment in the background.
